## 1. The water, the foam and what stays  (`#the-water-and-the-foam`)

Cited ayat: 13:17

> **13:17** أَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً فَسَالَتْ أَوْدِيَةٌۢ بِقَدَرِهَا فَٱحْتَمَلَ ٱلسَّيْلُ زَبَدًا رَّابِيًا وَمِمَّا يُوقِدُونَ عَلَيْهِ فِى ٱلنَّارِ ٱبْتِغَآءَ حِلْيَةٍ أَوْ مَتَٰعٍ زَبَدٌ مِّثْلُهُۥ كَذَٰلِكَ يَضْرِبُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْحَقَّ وَٱلْبَٰطِلَ فَأَمَّا ٱلزَّبَدُ فَيَذْهَبُ جُفَآءً وَأَمَّا مَا يَنفَعُ ٱلنَّاسَ فَيَمْكُثُ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ كَذَٰلِكَ يَضْرِبُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْأَمْثَالَ

### Claims

**c1** (13:17): God sent down water from the sky, so valleys flowed, each according to its measure, and the flood carried a swelling foam.

**c2** (13:17): From what they melt in the fire, seeking ornament or goods, there is foam like it.

**c3** (13:17): The ayah says that thus God strikes the truth and the falsehood.

**c4** (13:17): As for the foam, it goes as scum, while what benefits people stays in the earth; thus God strikes the similitudes.

### One-minute summary

God sent down water from the sky, and the flood carried a swelling foam [c1]. The foam goes as scum, while what benefits people stays in the earth [c4].

### Complete story

God sent down water from the sky, so valleys flowed, each according to its measure, and the flood carried a swelling foam [c1]. From what they melt in the fire, seeking ornament or goods, there is foam like it [c2]. The ayah says that thus God strikes the truth and the falsehood [c3]. As for the foam, it goes as scum, while what benefits people stays in the earth [c4]. Thus God strikes the similitudes [c4].

### Deep study

The ayah gives pictures that end alike: the flood of water and the melting of metals in the fire both leave foam [c1][c2]. It then states the point: the foam goes as scum and what benefits people stays [c4]. The ayah ties the pictures to the truth and the falsehood in its own words and does not spell out which part stands for which [c3][c4].

### Kids mode

God sent down water from the sky, and the valleys flowed with it [c1]. The flood carried foam [c1]. The foam goes away as scum, and what benefits people stays in the earth [c4].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayah sets what passes away, the foam, beside what stays, what benefits people, as a picture of falsehood and truth [c3][c4]. Another reading is that the ayah teaches by pictures of water and of fire that end in the same way [c1][c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: which part of the pictures stands for the truth and which for the falsehood; the ayah says that God strikes them thus and gives no list.
- Not established: what is melted, since the ayah says only what they melt in the fire seeking ornament or goods.
- The ayah itself says that God strikes the similitudes (amthal).
- The sense of awdiya as valleys and of zabad as foam is taken from common usage; a scholar may prefer other words.
